data.title: West Bank: Palestinians families trapped in home
data.description: Israeli settlers are carrying out a campaign of violence and intimidation against the Palestinian village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank, where families have had their electricity and water supplies cut off, in what residents say is an attempt to force them from their homes. The attacks came amid a sharp increase in settler violence in the West Bank following the October 7 Hamas attack, although villagers said such violence had been going on for years and was already making their lives increasingly difficult by 2023.

data.title: What does Clacton get for its loyalty to stroppy Nige? Next to nothing | John Crace
data.description: Why bother to improve people’s lives – or even show up – when getting votes is this easy? In many ways, though, the stunt hasn’t paid off What can Clacton possibly have done to deserve this? Is this some cosmic karma for a past existence in which the town executed hundreds of innocent women and children? Surely, even then, enough is enough. For the past few years Clacton seems to have been the centre of some abusive psychological experiment. The sort the Americans used to run in the 1950s and 60s, that have long since been banned. One run by Nigel Farage and designed merely to fuel his narcissistic dreams, with the voters mere cannon fodder. Clacton’s relationship with Nige is and always has been entirely one-sided. The town’s job is merely to vote for him, whenever he commands. Even for byelections that are entirely unnecessary and will possibly have to be re-run before the end of the year. On a turnout of just 44%, little more than 60% of the voters duly obliged on Thursday, even though none of the main parties were standing and Nige’s main opponent was a man with a bin on his head. Maybe parts of Clacton are waking up, and are fed up with Farage taking the piss out of them. Continue reading...

data.title: Nine life lessons from the happiest man in the world: from embracing tiny changes to not overthinking meditation
data.description: Stressed out, endlessly scrolling and never satisfied? Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche, the Buddhist monk with off-the-charts levels of contentment, may have the answers … By some metrics, Buddhist monk Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is the happiest man on Earth. In brain scans , researchers noted that Mingyur’s neural activity showed off-the-charts levels of activation in the left prefrontal cortex, an area associated with positive emotions such as happiness, enthusiasm and joy. In other tests conducted when he was 41 years old, his brain reportedly “ resembled that of a 33-year-old ”. He also laughs a lot. Can happiness be taught? I met Mingyur (Rinpoche is an honorary title meaning, roughly, “precious one”) to discover his strategies for a richer life. Continue reading...

data.title: Patriot missiles have been a godsend for Ukraine against Putin, but they’re running out. Kyiv needs help and fast | Jack Watling
data.description: Europe and Nato have known for years that interceptor production can’t keep up with demand and now disaster looms, putting us all in danger “Invincible.” That was how Vladimir Putin described Russia’s latest generation of ballistic missiles in 2018 . In 2022 he would unleash this arsenal to strike across Ukraine, hitting command centres, critical infrastructure and airfields. Then, in 2023, Ukraine received Patriot air defence systems from its international partners. The US-supplied missile interceptor would prove to be an effective shield against Russian strikes. But this year, supplies of Patriot missiles have run out and Kyiv has suffered the consequences. Intercepts have gone from more than 70% to none, so that night after night Russia strikes Ukraine’s infrastructure with impunity. This tragedy was long foretold, and there are no quick fixes. Jack Watling is senior research fellow for applied military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Disgraceful’: what one election photo tells us about British politics in 2026
data.description: Results from coastal town of Clacton have been interpreted positively by Nigel Farage and Count Binface, but one spoiled ballot tells its own story UK politics live – latest updates It ended, perhaps fittingly, on a rather baffling note. After 34 days of campaigning to regain the parliamentary seat of Clacton on England’s east coast, Nigel Farage, the leader of the Reform UK party, declined to turn up to the town’s leisure centre to hear himself declared the winner and MP. It was quite the thing. The last high-profile winning candidate to fail to enjoy his moment of victory was Bobby Sands in 1981. The IRA man had his reasons: he was on hunger strike in a prison in Northern Ireland, and went on to die 26 days later. Instead Farage attended a gathering of his supporters at an airfield on the outskirts of Clacton billed by his party as “Farage Fest”. He told fans he would be damned if he was going to stand on a stage “having won a resounding victory” and “be demeaned and humiliated by nobodies”. Continue reading...

data.title: El Niño may peak at the worst time for the Amazon – and it should worry us all
data.description: Delay to rainy season in forest already damaged by human-driven heating could trigger powerful ‘Godzilla’ El Niño As a supercharged climate scorches Europe with wildfire and deluges Asia with floods , the Amazon is bracing for a drought that strikes fear into the hearts of forest defenders and food producers alike. But it should worry even more of us. Scientists are predicting that the peak of El Niño will occur at the worst possible time for the world’s biggest tropical rainforest: the end of the dry season between October and December, when rivers are at their lowest and undergrowth is most likely to be tinder dry. This will be a period of extreme vulnerability for the forest, which plays a globally important role in stabilising the climate and irrigating crops. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’ve never done anything like this in my life’: Marina Abramović on making art with balloons
data.description: The artist’s latest swerve sees her creating an alien inflatable landscape for New York’s Balloon Museum Oversized inflatable blades of grass graze my face as I wind a path through the glowing white gallery space. Little papery squares of snow blow, some sticking to my hair. The path through the room curves so that only what is right in front of me is visible: initially, it seemed like I would reach the far side of the room in mere seconds but still my journey, magically, continues. I am at Snowy/Windy/Spring on Planet Z, the latest installation by the performance artist Marina Abramović . It opened earlier this month at New York’s newly opened Balloon Museum , which bills itself as “the first permanent home for inflatable art”. “I’ve never done anything like this in my life,” a smiling Abramović said, speaking on Zoom from her Manhattan apartment. “But if you give me an assignment then I’ll try to see what I can do with it.” As she began researching balloon art her first thought was that it was “so kitschy – basically for kids and games”. However, the more she contemplated the balloon, the more she saw its resonance with her own practice. “You put air in it, and at some point the air comes out. Or you pinch it and it disappears. The temporality of this is very close to what I’m doing: performance art.” Continue reading...

data.title: How the mob took Hollywood: the story of organized crime and the movies
data.description: Hollywood Crime Story: The Mob Takes Over the Movies looks back at how criminals insinuated themselves in the film business “From the foundation of Hollywood, organized crime is there.” So claims Tom Patterson, producer and director of new three-part documentary series, Hollywood Crime Story: The Mob Takes Over the Movies. Organized crime’s connection to the film industry actually predates Tinseltown, being present for the foundation of the medium itself, when inventor Thomas Edison sicced his hired goons on competitors in an attempt to maintain total control over early motion picture technology. As covered in Hollywood Crime Story, this resulted in said competitors – mostly Jewish businessmen from the east coast – fleeing westward and establishing the town and studio system that would become synonymous with movies as we know them. data.title: Why does everything feel meh? We're in the era of joyless decadence – Stateside with Kai and Carter
data.description: We should, in theory, be happy. Thanks to our phones, we can do practically anything – listen to our favorite bands' entire discographies, have extravagant meals delivered to our door, travel the world through an endless scroll. So why do so many of these experiences feel so joyless? Why do so many of us feel so empty all the time? Hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman wrestle with these questions with academics Michèle Mendelssohn and Charlie Tyson , who argue that we are living in an era of decadence without pleasure. While decadence always arises in times of extreme inequality, they say that tools like AI and GLP-1s reveal how we've lost our ability to truly enjoy things – and, ironically, reclaiming decadence may help us finally have fun. Michèle Mendelssohn and Charlie Tyson’s Guardian essay: Why does everything feel joyless? Welcome to the age of decadence without pleasure Continue reading...

data.title: Donald Trump can’t beat Iran and Nigel Farage can only beat a bin. When it counts, these populists are just losers | Jonathan Freedland
data.description: The pattern in the US and Britain is clear. They serve up stunt after stunt to mask incompetence and the betrayal of all those who trusted them It’s a shame Nigel Farage ducked the announcement of his victory in the Clacton byelection, which confirmed his return as MP for the seat he had needlessly resigned from just a few weeks earlier. You’d have thought he would have loved it. It was the culmination of a stunt, an exercise in politics as performance. It was a display animated by – and seeking to inflame – grievance, a million miles away from the hard, grinding work of tackling the problems that underlie those grievances. It was an attempt to deflect scrutiny, distract attention and evade responsibility. It was, in other words, everything nationalist populists like him excel at. Indeed, the only thing. Reform UK said Farage stayed away because Essex police had warned of a “ credible threat ” to his security, a claim swiftly denied by Essex police. (Add a flexible approach to the truth to that list of nationalist populists’ talents.) Still, it was a slightly odd claim to make. Recall Farage’s favoured explanation – there are others – for the undeclared £5m gift he received from the Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, which prompted the very parliamentary investigation that so riled the Reform leader he felt compelled to quit his seat and seek a preemptive not guilty verdict from the people of Clacton: namely, that he needed the money to pay for private, enhanced security. It seems £5m was not quite enough to ensure the lucky recipient would be safe standing next to a man dressed as a bin. Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: How can we talk about this extreme weather now that it’s a battleground in the culture wars? | Andy Beckett
data.description: Weather forecasts once gave Britons something safe to chat about. Not any more, and that’s a problem for the experts – indeed, for all of us In this fragmented but supposedly mild country, watching and talking about the weather forecast is meant to be a reassuring, unifying activity. Collectively, we have created and maintained a national climate narrative of small disappointments and pleasures. The first weather forecaster to appear on British TV, George Cowling, made his debut on the BBC in January 1954, predicting that “tomorrow would be rather windy”, but “a good day to hang out the washing”. For most of the 72 years since, such brief, carefully calibrated broadcasts have provided people from Aberdeen to Penzance with practical information, small talk and minor grumbles about essentially the same situation: living in a country where the weather is constantly changing, in a paradoxically unchanging way. Yet like the traditional British climate, that common weather culture may now be evaporating. “Met Office considers issuing red ‘extreme heat warning’ across Britain while nation enjoys ‘incredible summer’,” said the headline above the forecast on the GB News website on Monday, caught between terror and delight at the latest heatwave. As the climate crisis has affected this country in more and more unmistakable but uneven ways, TV weather forecasters have increasingly struggled to find the right language to describe this transformation’s daily consequences. Their struggle influences and exemplifies that of many Britons to understand, and work out what we think about, the apparent end of the weather patterns we expected to shape our whole lives. Andy Beckett is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Nigel Farage: Clacton cannot acquit him | Editorial
data.description: Reform won a contrived byelection, but scrutiny continues – while the party increasingly attacks the watchdogs and journalists asking awkward questions Nigel Farage didn’t attend the count of the byelection he forced upon Clacton. Instead, Reform UK’s leader celebrated his win with supporters at a “ Farage Fest ”, filmed by a friendly TV channel. For a politician who claims to speak for the people, it was telling that at his triumph he preferred an audience of believers. Mr Farage won because his toughest opponent on the campaign trail was a comedian in a jumpsuit with a bin on his head. That Count Binface nevertheless won 27% of the vote captured the absurdity of a contest the main parties had boycotted as a Faragist stunt. Reform UK’s leader wanted to turn scrutiny of his finances – notably an investigation into whether he failed to report a £5m gift from an overseas crypto billionaire – into a “fight” with the “establishment”. But the result determined who represents the Essex seat, not whether he broke parliamentary or electoral rules. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on booming poetry sales: Homer, meet the Instapoets | Editorial
data.description: In an unexpected twist, a Hollywood epic has contributed to Britain’s best-ever half-year in poetry sales In a short story called Career Move, published in the New Yorker in 1992, Martin Amis imagined a world in which screenwriters wrote for little magazines and earned a pittance while poets were global superstars. Amis’s story, a wonderfully ironic inversion of the time-honoured norm, was surprisingly prescient: the film and TV industries have been struggling, with screenwriters facing contracting outlets for their creations, whereas poets are now big business . The Bookseller reported recently that poetry sales were at a historic high . Part of the increase can be attributed to Christopher Nolan’s film The Odyssey, which has made Homer hot: editions of The Odyssey and its prequel, The Iliad, have garnered almost £1m in book sales in the UK this year. (As well as valiantly trying to keep the ailing film industry afloat, Nolan has also created a craze for epic poetry.) But Nolan’s film does not solely account for the boom in poetry sales. Even without the Homer run, sales of poetry texts and anthologies were still up by 7.2% from what was historically already a very high base. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Europe’s top clubs threatened Club World Cup boycott before Fifa plan collapsed
data.description: Ultimatum issued hours before plan was scrapped European Football Clubs demanded Infantino back down Europe’s leading clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless Gianni Infantino withdrew his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme, issuing their ultimatum hours before the plan was scrapped. In a letter to the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, the influential European Football Clubs (EFC) group warned that its cooperation with future tournaments would hinge on Infantino backing down. It said the threat would hold unless a joint venture between EFC and Fifa – a framework for which has already been agreed – is completed before television rights can be sold for the 2028 Women’s Club World Cup. data.title: Iga Swiatek takes swing at critics after ending title drought in Canada
data.description: Pole beats Rybakina to win her first title in 11 months but is angry about disapproving voices from her own country It came as no surprise that almost a year of pent-up emotion exploded from Iga Swiatek the moment she slotted her final backhand winner to clinch the Canadian Open title by defeating Elena Rybakina in two clean sets on Thursday night. As she screamed towards her team members on her corner of the court, pointed to her head and furiously pumped her fist, though, it was the tenor of Swiatek’s emotion that made her reaction noteworthy: she was angry. I think he was by far the best player in this league for the first six months [of the season] … but, with that being said, I’m feeling quite comfortable with us moving forward.” Continue reading...

data.title: Liverpool owner FSG seals £1.65bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
data.description: Confirmed deal values club as a whole at £5.5bn Amit Bhatia will become club’s new vice-chairman Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has confirmed it has agreed the sale of 30% of the club to a consortium including Amit Bhatia, the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and the Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin. The deal is understood to be worth £1.65bn, valuing Liverpool at £5.5bn, and will see Bhatia become the club’s new vice-chair on an expanded board. Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, initiated and led talks with FSG on behalf of the 1892 Holdings consortium, a reference to Liverpool’s founding year. The former co-owner of Queens Park Rangers has received financial backing from the Mittal Family Trust, the K5 Sports fund, of which Bezos is the lead investor, and EE Capital, the family office of Elaine and Eduardo Saverin. Continue reading...

data.title: Something Wile E this way comes: how the Looney Toons reboot movie came back from the dead
data.description: Cartoon royalty were lined for a live-action toon hybrid Coyote vs Acme. Then it was shelved as a tax write-off. But its cast, crew and fans fought for its release. Three years later it’s set to be a surprise summer hit Back in 2020, Dave Green started making his new film, Coyote vs Acme. Mixing live action with animation, it would be an unconventional courtroom drama that pitched actor Will Forte against a host of 2D Looney Tunes characters – including cartoon royalty such as Foghorn Leghorn, Porky Pig and Bugs Bunny. This, Green believed, would weave a heady spell for cinemagoers of all ages. Six years later, his film is finally about to be released. When Green first called “Action!”, his dark hair was not yet flecked liberally with grey. It is now. “We’ve held on to a lot of hope these past few years,” Green says from his home in Los Angeles, “and we never really let go of it.” Continue reading...

data.title: He Had It Coming review – this messy crime-comedy has all the subtlety of a mallet to the crotch
data.description: It’s sporadically very funny, but the tone of this blackly comic murder-mystery is all over the place. It wants to tackle big issues, but seems afraid of its own politics ‘But I can’t get an F,” wails Elise (Lydia West) in the first episode of the Australian campus comedy He Had It Coming, shoulders slumping like soufflés as her tutor peers pityingly at her terrible paintings. “I’m here on a scholarship? I’m here to be an artist ?! ” Alas, poor Elise. No amount of wounded upspeak can disguise the fact that she is an aspiring artist in much the same way a bag of flour is an aspiring pastry. Her “work”, bless it, consists of daubing clothes on to impressionist nudes – a “protest”, apparently, against the patriarchy and its preoccupation with “ancient bush”. Unctuous Professor Phoenix (Harry Greenwood) is unimpressed. “Hmm,” he sighs, pouting affectedly at Elise’s “feminist reimagining” of Manet’s Le Déjeuner sur l’herbe; the picnic’s enigmatic nude now sporting a pair of jeans and oversized novelty spectacles. Mon Dieu ! The problem, explains Phoenix, slowly, is a lack of ambition. Feminist art isn’t for amateurs . “Be radical,” he smirks, as Elise quietly broils with rage. “Don’t settle for mediocrity .” The nerve! “These men are holding us back,” she roars later at new pal Barbara (Natasha Liu Bordizzo), a prickly fashion influencer who is being slut-shamed by the campus jocks for having tipsily humped a stranger’s thigh at a party. “Yes,” agrees Barbara. “Let’s go vandalise something!” And so to the quadrant, where, in the dead of night, a mallet is applied to the genitals of the statue of the university’s hopelessly male namesake. He Had It Coming aired on BBC Three and is available on iPlayer in the UK and on Stan in Australia Continue reading...

Her “work”, bless it, consists of daubing clothes on to impressionist nudes – a “protest”, apparently, against the patriarchy and its preoccupation with “ancient bush”. Unctuous Professor Phoenix (Harry Greenwood) is unimpressed. “Hmm,” he sighs, pouting affectedly at Elise’s “feminist reimagining” of Manet’s Le Déjeuner sur l’herbe; the picnic’s enigmatic nude now sporting a pair of jeans and oversized novelty spectacles. Mon Dieu ! The problem, explains Phoenix, slowly, is a lack of ambition. Feminist art isn’t for amateurs . “Be radical,” he smirks, as Elise quietly broils with rage. “Don’t settle for mediocrity .” The nerve! “These men are holding us back,” she roars later at new pal Barbara (Natasha Liu Bordizzo), a prickly fashion influencer who is being slut-shamed by the campus jocks for having tipsily humped a stranger’s thigh at a party. “Yes,” agrees Barbara. “Let’s go vandalise something!” And so to the quadrant, where, in the dead of night, a mallet is applied to the genitals of the statue of the university’s hopelessly male namesake. He Had It Coming aired on BBC Three and is available on iPlayer in the UK and on Stan in Australia Continue reading...

data.title: Add to playlist: the heartbreak post-mortems of Cape Town’s Rowlene and the week’s best new tracks
data.description: The South African singer has been a memorable guest artist, but the unhurried, emotional tracks on new album Some Strings Attached show she’s ready for the spotlight From Cape Town, South Africa Recommended if you like Summer Walker, SZA, Shekhinah Up next Some Strings Attached out now Rowlene Bosman learned to sing in a Cape Town school choir, and the discipline never left her: she is a precision vocalist in a scene that rewards volume. Most South Africans first heard her in 2018, delivering the hook on Nasty C’s SMA – she was the first signing to his Tall Racks label – and the featured artist circuit kept her busy for years. But while South African pop stampeded towards amapiano, Rowlene held her ground as a balladeer, writing slow, confessional R&B in which heartbreak is examined instead of danced away. Her 2020 debut album 11:11, a set of aching, close-quarters soul songs, brought a South African music award nomination for best pop album, and three of her originals – Cupid , Stay and the Nasty C collaboration I Need You – landed on the soundtrack of Netflix’s SA teen crime drama Blood & Water, carrying her voice far beyond home. data.title: Hillborg: Lost Landscapes album review – sonic imagination and luminous colours
data.description: Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra/Kuusisto/Lubman/Falk Winland (Alpha) Unconventional instrumentation adds to the filmic feeling of these three works by the Swedish composer, played on this recording by a powerhouse orchestra on top form Anders Hillborg ’s stylistically eclectic work resists easy categorisation as these three rewarding works, performed by the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra, demonstrate. Lost Landscapes opens with signature glissandi , features a filmic, jazz-inflected chase and ends in an orchestral death spiral. Pekka Kuusisto draws out its luminous colours and richly clustered harmonies. The Strand Settings, a four-movement song cycle to texts by Canadian poet Mark Strand, was composed at the behest of Renée Fleming. Nature, the elements and a certain forlorn eroticism infuse poetry that Hillborg responds to with tonal and dynamic restraint. Gently pulsing strings with piquant woodwind and brass build atmospheric soundscapes over which Swedish soprano Ida Falk Winland spins haunting vocal lines in impeccable English. Continue reading...

data.title: Henry Threadgill, Vijay Iyer, Dafnis Prieto: Fifteen review – Pulitzer winner stirs gorgeous improv patterns
data.description: (Nonesuch) By turns gleeful, sensitive, urgent and ruminative, this is a brilliant set that plays to the trio’s formidable strengths Though the century-old Pulitzer prize – launched as a celebration of the craft and social necessity of good news reportage – was eventually expanded to include fiction and music by 1943, the US-born art of jazz has only been represented by Ornette Coleman and Wynton Marsalis in their lifetimes, Duke Ellington, John Coltrane and Thelonious Monk posthumously – and most recently Henry Threadgill , for his four-part suite In for a Penny, In for a Pound , in 2016. Publisher Joseph Pulitzer once declared his dreams for his readership were “to arrest their attention, enlist their sympathy … stimulate their imagination, convince their reason, and awaken their conscience”. Contemporary-classical composer and flautist Threadgill has been doing all that with his music, his personal story , his internationalism and his charisma since the 1960s. Now 82, he releases Fifteen, joining him in a brilliant trio featuring pianist/composer Vijay Iyer and creative Cuban percussionist Dafnis Prieto. Continue reading...

data.title: The best recent crime and thrillers – review roundup
data.description: The Amateur by Chris Bohjalian; Claws Out! by Bella Mackie; Plant Lady by Minyoung Kang; Children of Wolves by Lawrence Osborne; Mad Mabel by Sally Hepworth The Amateur by Chris Bohjalian (Hutchinson Heinemann, £18.99) American bestseller Bohjalian deserves to be far better known in the UK, although, as the first line of his 26th novel points out, “It is neither virtue nor might that rules the world; it’s luck”. Mira Winston’s luck began early, as she was born into a rich family, clever enough to secure a place at Yale, and a talented enough golfer to consider turning pro, but things change dramatically in 1978 when, at the age of 18, a ball she hits on a driving range smashes the temporal bone of a young caddy, killing him almost instantly. The freak accident turns out to be rather more complicated than first thought, not least because it becomes karmically conflated, in Mira’s mind, with her relationship with a married man twice her age. Told as a memoir, with Mira looking back on the derailment of her life and chronicling society’s changing perceptions of agency and privilege, this literary thriller is a masterfully executed ace. Claws Out! by Bella Mackie (Borough, £20) Mackie’s third novel centres on Diana, a manipulative grifter whose previous three husbands have died, apparently of natural causes. She’s in the process of getting her feet under the fourth mark’s prosperous Hampstead table when she encounters opposition. David Farrand’s “entitled but otherwise entirely average” daughter Catriona isn’t going to give up her father or her inheritance without a fight, and when she starts investigating Diana’s past, she discovers that her former stepchildren are convinced of foul play. Meanwhile, Diana’s own son, a feckless charmer, is also hoping to benefit from his mother’s matrimonial plans. Some readers may find the arch authorial tone grating, and the sharp-eyed will spot at least one major plot development before it occurs, but the incisive social satire, vinegary humour and expert pacing will keep you laughing as you turn the pages. Continue reading...

data.title: The Beverly Hills Housewife by James Cahill review – a trip inside Hockney’s world
data.description: Muse Betty Freeman sits at the centre of this sun-drenched book about art, eccentricity, and the spirit of Los Angeles David Hockney was 29 years old when he came to Betty Freeman’s house to photograph her swimming pool. Scouting locations for the pool paintings that would make him a household name, he took preparatory snaps of his partner, Peter Schlesinger, emerging naked from the water. And yet something about his aloof and quietly eccentric host, who dusted the hunting trophies while a handsome young man padded around her patio in the altogether, intrigued the artist. So he asked whether he might photograph her too, and she agreed. Completed a year later, Beverly Hills Housewife (1966/7) shows a beautiful woman standing outside a beautiful house. The scene is lit by an unbroken sun, her blond bob is undisturbed by any breeze, a lush fern sets off her popping pink dress. She is surrounded by the symbols of mid-century American prosperity: a chair by Le Corbusier, a tasteful modernist sculpture. We don’t need the title to know the place and time, because Hockney’s paintings have come to define them in our imagination: shimmering water and scattered light, bright colours and reflective surfaces, a clean and impassive contentment. Continue reading...

data.title: Alien: Isolation 2 – another strong female protagonist stalked in a terrifying new world
data.description: Creative Assembly could strike gold again with this follow-up to their fan-favourite, film-inspired game … if you’re brave enough to venture outdoors A lien: Isolation redefined Alien games on its release in 2014, bringing the original taut, haunted house theme of the first movie to fans who had mostly been fed action-packed shooters. Cowering under desks and inside lockers wasn’t a new thing; being hunted by an intelligent and lethal xenomorph that could spring down from a duct at any moment was. “I was thinking about what we could do for a sequel while we were still finishing the first game,” reveals Creative Assembly’s Alistair Hope, creative lead on Alien: Isolation and its sequel. “But we didn’t actually start the project until around the time of the 10th anniversary. We’ve seen the response grow over time, watching [Alien: Isolation] continue to find new players, even though it’s a relatively old game. And they’re surprised there isn’t a sequel.” Continue reading...

data.title: Rebecca Perry: ‘Lorca hit me like a bolt of lightning’
data.description: The poet and novelist on the power of fairytales, being inspired by Frank O’Hara and the joys of Doris Lessing My earliest reading memory Reading On the Ning Nang Nong by Spike Milligan, aged five or so, sitting on the floor of the bedroom I shared with my brother – who, in my memory, was sitting on the carpet next to me. My favourite book growing up I had a collection of fairytales in a big yellow hardback, which I was totally entranced by from around the age of seven to 10. I’ll never forget the feeling of despair on turning the page and discovering that the Little Mermaid had become foam on the surface of the water; it was a very early lesson in the helplessness of the reader in the face of a story’s destiny. In particular, though, I loved a Scottish fairytale called The Black Bull of Norroway, which I think, in many ways, has been under the surface of everything I’ve ever written. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Murakami saw his book come alive!’: the Japanese company bringing the author’s science fiction masterpiece to the stage
data.description: A play based on the writer’s dreamlike novel Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World is touring the world, riding a wave of interest in Japanese culture. Its creators talk about how they adapted the famously cryptic tale Tatsuya Fujiwara is no stranger to London’s Barbican theatre. It was here nearly 30 years ago that one of Japan’s biggest film stars, now 44, made his stage debut. He was just 15, plucked out of an audition of more than 5,000 hopeful youngsters by the revered theatre director Yukio Ninagawa for his play Shintoku-Maru. It kickstarted Fujiwara’s career, and three years later he landed a role in the cult dystopian film Battle Royale, going on to star in hit TV dramas and blockbuster films, all the while continuing to perform in Ninagawa’s acclaimed productions. Now, Fujiwara returns to where it all began, to perform in a stage adaptation of Haruki Murakami’s science fiction novel Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World. The story alternates between two seemingly unrelated narratives: a cyberpunk thriller set in Tokyo, and a surreal fantasy that unfolds within a mysterious walled town. Directed by the French choreographer Philippe Decouflé, the play premiered in Tokyo in January, toured Japan until March, then Singapore in April. After the Barbican run this autumn, the tour will wrap up in Paris. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I felt so inspired’: Guardian readers on trying Homer’s epics after seeing The Odyssey
data.description: Readers describe how Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster has ignited or reawakened their interest in classical literature “I’m having a classics summer this year,” says Tommy Maddinson, 26, from London. He’s been inspired by Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey to delve into the subject, which has involved cinema trips, visits to the British Museum, and reading Homer’s epic before the film’s release. “I managed to finish it the day before. Since then I’ve been reading a few other classical texts and commentaries …” Maddinson is not alone. Thanks to the popularity of Nolan’s film, poetry sales in the UK are on course to reach a record high this year after surpassing £8m during the first 30 weeks of 2026 – an increase of 13.3% on the same period last year, according to the market researchers NielsenIQ. data.title: Iris Murdoch artworks from secret room go on display – including self-portrait
data.description: Second world war paintings and sketches show novelist ‘engaging with her world in a new light’ For decades, they lay in a secret room in her attic gathering dust. Now, newly discovered artworks by the Booker prize-winning author Iris Murdoch – including the only self-portrait she is known to have painted, four surrealist landscape paintings and three sketches of female nudes – will go on display for the first time on Friday. The artworks were created at the start of the second world war when Murdoch was a student at Oxford. They expose her early interest in surrealism and fascination with the naked female form. data.title: Why is Drake barking like a dog? Six things you need to know about the rapper’s midlife pivot
data.description: There’s a lot to unpack as this proud son of Toronto closes in on 40 – from his gambling to his very public dates. Here goes! Even if you can only name a handful of rappers, Drake is probably one of them. Not so many years ago, he was among the planet’s biggest celebrities, named in the same breath as Taylor Swift and Beyoncé and breaking chart records set by the Beatles. Many of his dozens of hit singles – Work, One Dance, Hotline Bling and God’s Plan – were ubiquitous, among the last truly crossover radio hits. Drake is still landing chart spots ( if not critical acclaim ), but now it’s his foray into the “creator economy” that’s raising eyebrows – shilling for a crypto casino , fraternising with manosphere influencers and, just last weekend, live-streaming dates with OnlyFans models. So what’s this all about? Is Toronto’s once-golden boy having a midlife crisis – or is it a media-savvy pivot? Here’s how Drake got caught up in the “creator economy”. Continue reading...

The fruit can even be cooked a day in advance, leaving little more to do than whip everything together before freezing. Thanks to the condensed milk, the cream freezes surprisingly softly, while the meringue keeps its gentle chew and the toasted coconut adds a welcome crunch and nuttiness. data.title: Male redback spiders somersault directly towards a female’s fangs during mating
data.description: Recent research uncovers that a singular genetic region governs the intricate somersaulting behavior of male redback spiders during mating rituals. This fascinating behavior, crucial for reproduction, is inherited through the X chromosome. Experimental hybrids indicate that this somersault characteristic is not only recessive but also X-linked. Conversely, abdominal narrowing seems influenced by a combination of multiple genes and environmental conditions, challenging traditional views on the complexity of genetic traits.

data.translatedDescription: A powerful earthquake with several aftershocks struck has hit Indonesia, damaging buildings and triggering a tsunami warning.

data.title: Local family wins keys to $3.5m Bondi semi as bidder fails to show
data.description: A registered bidder decided not to attend the auction at the last moment in hope that the three-bedroom property would pass in. It didn’t work out that way.
data.translatedTitle: Local family wins keys to $3.5m Bondi semi as bidder fails to show
data.translatedDescription: A registered bidder decided not to attend the auction at the last moment in hope that the three-bedroom property would pass in. It didn’t work out that way.

data.title: Sam Short narrowly misses world record
data.description: Australian Sam Short clocks a new lifetime best and the fastest time ever swum in a US pool in the men's 400m freestyle, but just misses out on a new world record time.
data.translatedTitle: Sam Short narrowly misses world record
data.translatedDescription: Australian Sam Short clocks a new lifetime best and the fastest time ever swum in a US pool in the men's 400m freestyle, but just misses out on a new world record time.

data.title: Lani Pallister beats swimming idol for gold
data.description: Australian distance star Lani Pallister wins gold and beats her idol, USA's Katie Ledecky in the women's 400m freestyle in Irvine, California.
data.translatedTitle: Lani Pallister beats swimming idol for gold
data.translatedDescription: Australian distance star Lani Pallister wins gold and beats her idol, USA's Katie Ledecky in the women's 400m freestyle in Irvine, California.

data.title: Dans le classement de Shanghaï 2026, la France se maintient et la Chine progresse
data.description: La France compte, comme en 2025, 27 universités dans le classement rendu public samedi 15 août, dont quatre dans le top 100. Les universités chinoises gagnent des places dans un palmarès toujours dominé par les établissements anglo-saxons.
data.translatedTitle: In the Shanghai 2026 ranking, France maintains its position and China progresses
data.translatedDescription: France has, as in 2025, 27 universities in the ranking made public on Saturday August 15, including four in the top 100. Chinese universities are gaining places in a ranking still dominated by Anglo-Saxon establishments.

data.title: Donald Trump fait réagir Téhéran en déclarant vouloir proclamer le détroit d’Ormuz « territoire des Etats-Unis » après la guerre
data.description: « Le détroit d’Ormuz (…) restera iranien », a répliqué, samedi 15 août, Kazem Gharibabadi, vice-ministre des affaires étrangères iranien. Le président américain avait ajouté, lors d’un meeting tenu la veille, qu’il ne « s’excuserait jamais » d’avoir déclenché la guerre avec l’Iran malgré son impact sur les cours du pétrole.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump makes Tehran react by declaring that he wants to proclaim the Strait of Hormuz “territory of the United States” after the war
data.translatedDescription: “The Strait of Hormuz (…) will remain Iranian,” replied Kazem Gharibabadi, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister, on Saturday August 15. The American president added, during a meeting held the day before, that he would “never apologize” for starting the war with Iran despite its impact on oil prices.

data.title: EN DIRECT, incendies et canicule : le feu dans les Landes a parcouru 1 300 hectares ; 83 départements en vigilance orange
data.description: Sur le front de la canicule, les fortes chaleurs régresseront samedi dans l’Ouest, mais persisteront en revanche sur la moitié est et sur l’Ile-de-France, avec encore 35 ºC à 39 ºC attendus. Au sud de Rennes, à Saint-Just, 230 hectares de forêt ont été parcourus par le feu depuis mercredi, mais la progression de l’incendie a été ralentie.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, fires and heatwave: the fire in the Landes covered 1,300 hectares; 83 departments on orange alert
data.translatedDescription: On the heatwave front, the intense heat will decrease on Saturday in the West, but will however persist in the eastern half and in Ile-de-France, with still 35ºC to 39ºC expected. South of Rennes, in Saint-Just, 230 hectares of forest have been covered by fire since Wednesday, but the progression of the fire has been slowed down.

data.title: En Afghanistan, les talibans ont rompu leur isolement international, cinq ans après leur retour au pouvoir
data.description: Les capitales des pays voisins discutent avec Kaboul des circuits commerciaux régionaux tandis qu’Américains et Européens négocient avec le régime au nom de la lutte contre le terrorisme et pour le retour dans le pays de déboutés du droit d’asile.
data.translatedTitle: In Afghanistan, the Taliban have broken their international isolation, five years after their return to power
data.translatedDescription: The capitals of neighboring countries are discussing regional trade circuits with Kabul while Americans and Europeans are negotiating with the regime in the name of the fight against terrorism and for the return to the country of those whose right to asylum has been rejected.

data.title: Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans : le Conseil constitutionnel inflige un camouflet à l’exécutif
data.description: Le Conseil constitutionnel a jugé qu’en s’appliquant à tous les réseaux sociaux et à tous les mineurs sans distinction, la loi enfreignait la liberté d’expression. Emmanuel Macron a chargé son gouvernement d’aboutir à un nouveau texte avant la fin de son mandat.
data.translatedTitle: Ban on social networks for under 15s: the Constitutional Council inflicts a snub on the executive
data.translatedDescription: The Constitutional Council ruled that by applying to all social networks and all minors without distinction, the law violated freedom of expression. Emmanuel Macron tasked his government with arriving at a new text before the end of his mandate.

data.title: La fête de l’Assomption, ou l’histoire politique d’une dévotion française à la Vierge Marie
data.description: Le 15 août occupe une place particulière en France depuis le « vœu » de Louis XIII en 1638, qui consacra son royaume à la Vierge et instaura sa célébration. Ce geste, qui reflète des siècles de référence monarchique à la mère du Christ, a conservé une résonance politique jusqu’à nos jours.
data.translatedTitle: The Feast of the Assumption, or the political history of a French devotion to the Virgin Mary
data.translatedDescription: August 15 has held a special place in France since the “vow” of Louis XIII in 1638, who dedicated his kingdom to the Virgin and established its celebration. This gesture, which reflects centuries of monarchical reference to the mother of Christ, has retained a political resonance until today.

data.title: Indonésie : un puissant séisme fait un mort ; pas de risque de tsunami
data.description: Dans les provinces du Nusa Tenggara oriental, occidental, et du Sulawesi du Sud, où des habitants ont été appelés à évacuer, les autorités ont finalement levé l’alerte au tsunami déclenchée par un tremblement de terre d’une magnitude de 7,7.
data.translatedTitle: Indonesia: powerful earthquake leaves one dead; no risk of tsunami
data.translatedDescription: In the provinces of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, and South Sulawesi, where residents were called to evacuate, authorities finally lifted the tsunami alert triggered by a 7.7 magnitude earthquake.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : plusieurs régions russes rationnent le carburant après les frappes ukrainiennes
data.description: Le gouvernement russe a confirmé que l’approvisionnement des stations-service en carburant restait « tendu » dans plusieurs zones du pays. Selon un décompte de Bloomberg effectué à partir des déclarations publiques des deux camps, l’Ukraine a attaqué 11 des 34 grandes raffineries russes depuis le début du mois.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, war in Ukraine: several Russian regions ration fuel after Ukrainian strikes
data.translatedDescription: The Russian government has confirmed that fuel supplies to gas stations remain “tight” in several areas of the country. According to a Bloomberg tally based on public statements from both sides, Ukraine has attacked 11 of Russia's 34 major refineries since the start of the month.

data.title: Le Conseil constitutionnel valide la loi sur la fin de vie, les établissements catholiques obtiennent leur « clause de conscience »
data.description: Dans une décision rendue vendredi 14 août, l’institution assure « la liberté personnelle » d’un malade d’accéder à l’administration d’une substance létale à sa demande et après accord d’un médecin. En revanche, la décision exempte les établissements privés et associatifs de l’obligation de permettre la réalisation d’une aide à mourir dans leurs murs.
data.translatedTitle: The Constitutional Council validates the law on the end of life, Catholic establishments obtain their “conscience clause”
data.translatedDescription: In a decision rendered on Friday August 14, the institution ensures “the personal freedom” of a patient to access the administration of a lethal substance at their request and after agreement from a doctor. On the other hand, the decision exempts private and associative establishments from the obligation to allow assistance in dying to be carried out within their walls.

data.title: « On m’a offert une poupée sur un poney, entourée de dessins de phallus » : le pot de départ graveleux de Marine, employée dans le BTP
data.description: « Bon vent ! » (11/18). Elle ne supportait plus le sexisme ordinaire et l’ambiance potache de cette entreprise du BTP. Marine, 31 ans, n’avait encore rien vu…
data.translatedTitle: “I was given a doll on a pony, surrounded by drawings of phallus”: the gritty parting of Marine, employed in the construction industry
data.translatedDescription: “Good luck! » (11/18). She could no longer stand the ordinary sexism and schoolboy atmosphere of this construction company. Marine, 31, hadn’t seen anything yet…

data.title: Cyclisme : le jeune Gallois Finlay Tarling tué dans un accident au Tour du Portugal
data.description: Selon la télévision publique RTP, le coureur britannique de 19 ans de l’équipe NSN Development a été percuté pendant la 8ᵉ étape, vendredi, par une voiture circulant en sens inverse, un peu en retrait du peloton.
data.translatedTitle: Cycling: young Welshman Finlay Tarling killed in accident at Tour of Portugal
data.translatedDescription: According to public television RTP, the 19-year-old British rider from the NSN Development team was hit during the 8th stage on Friday by a car traveling in the opposite direction, a little behind the peloton.

data.title: « On est en train de perdre notre jeunesse » : dans le nord du Maroc, l’ombre des noyés de Ceuta
data.description: A Tétouan, les familles se désespèrent après la mort de nombreux hommes qui ont tenté le passage à la nage jusqu’à l’enclave espagnole, fin juillet. Au total, plus de 140 d’entre eux auraient perdu la vie, selon une ONG marocaine. Malgré ces drames, beaucoup rêvent encore de gagner clandestinement l’Europe.
data.translatedTitle: “We are losing our youth”: in the north of Morocco, the shadow of the drowned people of Ceuta
data.translatedDescription: In Tetouan, families are in despair after the death of numerous men who attempted to swim to the Spanish enclave at the end of July. In total, more than 140 of them lost their lives, according to a Moroccan NGO. Despite these tragedies, many still dream of reaching Europe clandestinely.

data.title: Luigi Mangione admet avoir tiré sur le PDG d’UnitedHealthcare et plaide coupable de harcèlement criminel
data.description: « J’ai tiré sur M. Thompson, et il est mort », a déclaré le jeune homme devant le tribunal fédéral, ajoutant qu’il savait que ce qu’il faisait était illégal.
data.translatedTitle: Luigi Mangione admits to shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO, pleads guilty to stalking
data.translatedDescription: “I shot Mr. Thompson, and he died,” the young man testified in federal court, adding that he knew what he was doing was illegal.

data.title: Au Venezuela, plus de 130 prisonniers politiques libérés après le rapprochement entre le pouvoir et l’opposition
data.description: Le chef de la diplomatie américaine, Marco Rubio, a salué « une étape cruciale dans le processus de réconciliation nationale », alors que Washington supervise la phase de discussions entre le gouvernement vénézuélien et des représentants de l’opposition.
data.translatedTitle: In Venezuela, more than 130 political prisoners released after rapprochement between power and opposition
data.translatedDescription: The head of American diplomacy, Marco Rubio, welcomed “a crucial step in the process of national reconciliation”, while Washington supervises the phase of discussions between the Venezuelan government and representatives of the opposition.

data.title: Au Tchad, neuf opposants, dont Succès Masra, libérés après avoir été graciés par le président Mahamat Idriss Déby
data.description: Ancien premier ministre et chef du principal parti d’opposition, Succès Masra purgeait depuis plus d’un an une peine de vingt ans de prison ferme. Les huit autres dirigeants de partis étaient condamnés car accusés de fomenter une insurrection.
data.translatedTitle: In Chad, nine opponents, including Succès Masra, released after being pardoned by President Mahamat Idriss Déby
data.translatedDescription: Former prime minister and leader of the main opposition party, Succès Masra had been serving a twenty-year prison sentence for more than a year. The eight other party leaders were convicted on charges of fomenting an insurrection.

data.title: Chez les opposants à Gianni Infantino, les grandes manœuvres sont lancées pour faire tomber le président de la FIFA
data.description: Trois confédérations continentales, dont l’UEFA, aspirent à changer les statuts de la Fédération internationale de football afin de pousser vers la sortie son patron contesté, fragilisé par son projet avorté de création d’une société commerciale.
data.translatedTitle: Among Gianni Infantino's opponents, major maneuvers are launched to bring down the FIFA president
data.translatedDescription: Three continental confederations, including UEFA, aspire to change the statutes of the International Football Federation in order to push out its contested boss, weakened by his aborted project to create a commercial company.

data.title: Frist für Iran-USA-Abkommen verstreicht – Naher Osten vor ungewisser Zukunft
data.description: Während US-Präsident Trump mit einer Übernahme der Straße von Hormus kokettiert, gehen die Angriffe auf zivile Schiffe weiter. Dabei sollte in diesen Tagen ein finales Abkommen stehen.
data.translatedTitle: Deadline for Iran-USA agreement has passed – the Middle East faces an uncertain future
data.translatedDescription: While US President Trump flirts with a takeover of the Strait of Hormuz, attacks on civilian ships continue. A final agreement should be reached in these days.

data.title: USS »Abraham Lincoln«: Donald Trump findet, Einsatz auf Flugzeugträger dauert »noch nicht lange genug«
data.description: Seit mehr als acht Monaten ist der Flugzeugträger im Nahen Osten, es gibt Versorgungsengpässe, die Besatzung ist offenbar am Limit. Ein Problem sieht der US-Präsident darin nicht.
data.translatedTitle: USS "Abraham Lincoln": Donald Trump thinks that deployment on an aircraft carrier "doesn't last long enough"
data.translatedDescription: The aircraft carrier has been in the Middle East for more than eight months, there are supply bottlenecks and the crew is apparently at its limit. The US President does not see this as a problem.

data.title: USS »Abraham Lincoln«: Lassen die USA die Besatzung des Flugzeugträgers im Stich?
data.description: Seit mehr als acht Monaten harren 5000 Besatzungsmitglieder an Bord des Flugzeugträgers USS »Abraham Lincoln« aus. Die Versorgungslage ist prekär, die psychische Belastung enorm. Wann die Ablösung kommt, ist offen. Der Überblick.
data.translatedTitle: USS “Abraham Lincoln”: Is the USA abandoning the crew of the aircraft carrier?
data.translatedDescription: 5,000 crew members have been waiting on board the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln for more than eight months. The supply situation is precarious and the psychological strain is enormous. It is unclear when the replacement will come. The overview.

data.title: News: Waldbrände in Deutschland, Machtübernahme der Taliban, Russlands Krieg gegen ukrainische Zivilisten
data.description: Hunderte Feuerwehrkräfte kämpfen gegen den Waldbrand in der Eifel. Die Taliban sind seit fünf Jahren an der Macht. Und Russland zielt auf ukrainische Tankstellen. Das ist die Lage am Samstagmorgen.
data.translatedTitle: News: Forest fires in Germany, the Taliban coming to power, Russia's war against Ukrainian civilians
data.translatedDescription: Hundreds of firefighters are fighting the forest fire in the Eifel. The Taliban have been in power for five years. And Russia is targeting Ukrainian gas stations. This is the situation on Saturday morning.

data.title: Hürtgenwald in der Eifel: Bewohner warten auf Evakuierung wegen Waldbrand
data.description: »Dein Haus ist in den Nachrichten«, schreibt der Enkel am Morgen, da herrscht bei der Oma bereits panische Angst. Ein Großfeuer im Hürtgenwald rückt an die Dörfer heran, Menschen warten auf die Evakuierung – und darauf, dass der Wind dreht.
data.translatedTitle: Hürtgenwald in the Eifel: Residents are waiting to be evacuated due to forest fire
data.translatedDescription: “Your house is in the news,” the grandson writes in the morning, and Grandma is already panicking. A major fire in the Hürtgen Forest is approaching the villages, people are waiting for the evacuation - and for the wind to change.

data.title: Feuer im Hürtgenwald: Feuerwehr muss Einsatzzentrale wegen Rauch verlegen – Löscharbeiten gingen in der Nacht weiter
data.description: Der Hürtgenwald in der Eifel steht weiter in Flammen. Die Einsatzleitung der Feuerwehr musste umziehen, um dem Qualm auszuweichen. Die Brandbekämpfer rechnen mit einem Einsatz, der noch Tage dauern wird.
data.translatedTitle: Fire in the Hürtgenwald: Fire brigade has to relocate the operations center due to smoke - extinguishing work continued during the night
data.translatedDescription: The Hürtgen Forest in the Eifel is still in flames. The fire department's operations management had to move to avoid the smoke. The fire fighters expect an operation that will take days.

data.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Wie Campact mit drei Millionen Euro gegen die AfD mobilisiert
data.description: Die Plattform Campact will mit Millionenspenden eine Alleinregierung der AfD verhindern, indem sie SPD und Grünen den Einzug in den Landtag sichert. Ein ähnlicher Aufruf war schon einmal erfolgreich.
data.translatedTitle: Saxony-Anhalt: How Campact is mobilizing against the AfD with three million euros
data.translatedDescription: The Campact platform wants to use millions in donations to prevent the AfD from forming a sole government by securing the SPD and Greens' entry into the state parliament. A similar call has already been successful.

data.title: Stendal: AfD-Politiker verfolgt 14-Jährigen mit Baseballschläger
data.description: In Stendal haben zwei Jugendliche ein AfD-Wahlplakat beschädigt. Dabei lauerten ihnen zwei Politiker der rechtsextremen Partei auf. Ein 14-Jähriger wurde verletzt. Die Polizei ermittelt.
data.translatedTitle: Stendal: AfD politician pursues 14-year-old with baseball bat
data.translatedDescription: In Stendal, two young people damaged an AfD election poster. Two politicians from the right-wing extremist party ambushed them. A 14-year-old was injured. The police are investigating.

data.title: Jason Arday: Cambridge-Professor nach Plagiatsvorwürfen tot aufgefunden
data.description: Er war der jüngste schwarze Professor an der Eliteuniversität Cambridge, nach Plagiatsvorwürfen legt er sein Amt nieder. Nun ist Jason Arday tot. Seine Familie erhebt schwere Vorwürfe.
data.translatedTitle: Jason Arday: Cambridge professor found dead after plagiarism allegations
data.translatedDescription: He was the youngest black professor at the elite University of Cambridge, but he resigned from his position after allegations of plagiarism. Jason Arday is now dead. His family is making serious allegations.

data.title: Klima: KI führt laut Studie zu mehr Emissionen aus Kohle, Öl und Gas
data.description: Künstliche Intelligenz kann bei der Energiewende helfen – oder dem Klima schaden. Neue Studien kommen zu einem eindeutig negativen Schluss. Das Ausmaß des Problems zeigt sich gerade in Nordrhein-Westfalen.
data.translatedTitle: Climate: According to the study, AI leads to more emissions from coal, oil and gas
data.translatedDescription: Artificial intelligence can help with the energy transition – or harm the climate. New studies come to a clearly negative conclusion. The extent of the problem is particularly evident in North Rhine-Westphalia.

data.title: Donald Trump: So verlief die Flucht im Catering-Container
data.description: Mit einem Täuschungsmanöver wurde US-Präsident Trump vor einem angeblich drohenden iranischen Anschlag in Sicherheit gebracht. Der Rest seiner Delegation blieb als argloser »Köder« zurück. Die Rekonstruktion.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump: This is how the escape in the catering container went
data.translatedDescription: With a deceptive maneuver, US President Trump was brought to safety from an allegedly impending Iranian attack. The rest of his delegation remained as unsuspecting “bait.” The reconstruction.

data.title: Zwei Flugzeuge mit gleicher Nummer fliegen aufeinander zu – Lotse verhindert Kollision
data.description: In den USA hat ein Fluglotse nur knapp eine Katastrophe verhindert. Wegen eines Fehlers waren zwei Boeing mit derselben Flugnummer unterwegs. Anweisungen zur Flugroute galten daher für beide Jets – bis ein Lotse eingriff.
data.translatedTitle: Two aircraft with the same number fly towards each other - the controller prevents a collision
data.translatedDescription: In the USA, an air traffic controller narrowly prevented a disaster. Due to an error, two Boeings were traveling with the same flight number. Instructions regarding the flight route therefore applied to both jets – until a controller intervened.

data.title: Bauarbeiter finden in Belgien Gold im Wert von neun Millionen Euro
data.description: Ungläubigkeit und Staunen – so beschreibt ein Arbeiter den Moment, als sein Team beim Verlegen eines Abwasserrohrs auf einen Goldschatz stieß. Neun Millionen Euro, eingemauert in einer Kellerwand in einem Haus in Belgien.
data.translatedTitle: Construction workers find gold worth nine million euros in Belgium
data.translatedDescription: Disbelief and amazement – ​​this is how a worker describes the moment when his team came across a treasure of gold while laying a sewer pipe. Nine million euros, walled up in a basement wall in a house in Belgium.

data.title: Selena Gomez: Start-up wird auf Millionen verklagt
data.description: Gemeinsam mit ihrer Mutter gründete Selena Gomez »Wondermind«, eine Plattform für mentale Gesundheit. Nun verklagen zwei Investoren die Gründerinnen. Der Vorwurf: Sie hätten mit falschen Versprechen gelockt.
data.translatedTitle: Selena Gomez: Start-up is being sued for millions
data.translatedDescription: Together with her mother, Selena Gomez founded "Wondermind", a platform for mental health. Now two investors are suing the founders. The accusation: They lured people with false promises.

data.title: Matisse, Renoir und Cézanne: Drei aus Museen in Italien gestohlene Gemälde wieder aufgetaucht
data.description: Mitten in der Nacht verschwinden drei Kunstwerke, zusammen sind sie fast zehn Millionen Euro wert: Nach monatelangen Ermittlungen kann die italienische Polizei nun einen Erfolg vermelden.
data.translatedTitle: Matisse, Renoir and Cézanne: Three paintings stolen from museums in Italy resurfaced
data.translatedDescription: Three works of art disappear in the middle of the night; together they are worth almost ten million euros: after months of investigation, the Italian police can now report a success.

data.title: Helmut Lethen: Kulturwissenschaftler im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben
data.description: Mit seiner Epochenstudie »Verhaltenslehren der Kälte« wurde er in den Neunzigerjahren zum Kultautor. Jetzt ist Helmut Lethen im Alter von 87 Jahren gestorben.
data.translatedTitle: Helmut Lethen: cultural scientist died at the age of 87
data.translatedDescription: He became a cult author in the 1990s with his epochal study “The Behavioral Lessons of the Cold.” Helmut Lethen has now died at the age of 87.

data.title: Rostock: Ehepaar kann laut Landgericht Geld zurückverlangen, weil FKK-Bereich auf Kreuzfahrtschiff kleiner war
data.description: Eine Weltreise per Kreuzfahrtschiff wollte ein Paar auch im FKK-Bereich genießen. Sie wurden aber von Größe und Ausstattung enttäuscht und forderten einen Teil der Kosten zurück. Ein Gericht gab ihnen recht – aber nicht ganz.
data.translatedTitle: Rostock: According to the district court, the couple can demand money back because the nudist area on the cruise ship was smaller
data.translatedDescription: A couple also wanted to enjoy a nudist trip around the world on a cruise ship. However, they were disappointed by the size and features and demanded part of the costs back. A court agreed with them – but not entirely.

data.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Owen Ansah holt Gold, Emil Agyekum und Shanice Kraft Silber
data.description: Sprinter Owen Ansah hat in Birmingham das dritte EM-Gold für das deutsche Team gewonnen. Fraglich bleibt, ob er den Titel behalten darf. Jeweils Silber holten Hürdenläufer Emil Agyekum und Diskuswerferin Shanice Kraft.
data.translatedTitle: European Athletics Championships: Owen Ansah takes gold, Emil Agyekum and Shanice Kraft take silver
data.translatedDescription: Sprinter Owen Ansah won the third European Championship gold for the German team in Birmingham. It remains questionable whether he will be allowed to keep the title. Hurdler Emil Agyekum and discus thrower Shanice Kraft each took silver.

data.title: Schwimm-EM: Isabel Gose, Angelina Köhler und Maya Werner bejubeln Medaillen
data.description: Ex-Weltmeisterin Angelina Köhler versöhnt sich mit Paris. Isabel Gose steht zum vierten Mal auf dem Podest, wieder neben Maya Werner. Für Olympiasieger Lukas Märtens war sein Rennen vorbei, »ehe ich gefühlt im Wasser war«.
data.translatedTitle: European Swimming Championships: Isabel Gose, Angelina Köhler and Maya Werner celebrate medals
data.translatedDescription: Former world champion Angelina Köhler reconciles with Paris. Isabel Gose is on the podium for the fourth time, again next to Maya Werner. For Olympic champion Lukas Märtens, his race was over “before I felt like I was in the water.”

data.title: Reit-WM 2026: Debütantin Katharina Hemmer holt überraschend Bronze
data.description: Zwei Tage nach dem WM-Titel im Team sichert sich Katharina Hemmer die Bronzemedaille im Grand Prix Special. Isabell Werth muss sich mit Rang vier begnügen. Auch die Vielseitigkeitsreiter sind auf Medaillenkurs.
data.translatedTitle: Equestrian World Championships 2026: Debutant Katharina Hemmer surprisingly wins bronze
data.translatedDescription: Two days after winning the World Championship title in the team, Katharina Hemmer secured the bronze medal in the Grand Prix Special. Isabell Werth has to be content with fourth place. The eventing riders are also on course for medals.

data.title: FC Liverpool: Jeff Bezos sichert sich Minderheitsbeteiligung
data.description: Als Teil eines Konsortiums hat sich der Amazon-Milliardär beim FC Liverpool eingekauft – für einen Betrag von bis zu 1,8 Milliarden Euro. Fans machen sich Sorgen um die Zukunft des Premier-League-Clubs.
data.translatedTitle: Liverpool FC: Jeff Bezos secures minority stake
data.translatedDescription: As part of a consortium, the Amazon billionaire bought into Liverpool FC – for an amount of up to 1.8 billion euros. Fans are worried about the future of the Premier League club.

data.title: Nathalie Pohl: Extremschwimmerin erreicht nach vier Tagen und 200 Kilometern Köln
data.description: Am Dienstag ist Nathalie Pohl in den Main gesprungen, an diesem Freitag ist die 31-Jährige nun in Köln aus dem Rhein gestiegen. Mit der Aktion will Pohl für die Sicherheit junger Schwimmer werben.
data.translatedTitle: Nathalie Pohl: Extreme swimmer reaches Cologne after four days and 200 kilometers
data.translatedDescription: On Tuesday, Nathalie Pohl jumped into the Main, and this Friday the 31-year-old got out of the Rhine in Cologne. Pohl wants to use the campaign to promote the safety of young swimmers.

data.title: DDR-Moped: Auch reimportierte Simsons dürfen Tempo 60 fahren
data.description: Schwalben, Stare oder Sperber fahren schneller als Mopeds aus dem Westen – legal, wenn sie aus der DDR-Zeit übrig geblieben sind. Nun wird die Simson-Sonderregel ausgeweitet.
data.translatedTitle: GDR moped: Reimported Simsons are also allowed to drive at 60 km/h
data.translatedDescription: Swallows, starlings and sparrowhawks drive faster than mopeds from the West - legally if they are left over from the GDR era. Now the Simson special rule is being expanded.

data.title: Kleingarten: »Sogar Wessis sind Menschen« – Streit im Schrebergarten - SPIEGEL TV
data.description: Ein Schrebergarten soll ein Ort der Idylle sein. Nicht so im beschaulichen Teil Leipzigs. Hier eskaliert der Klassenkampf. Es geht um einen Parkplatz samt Gebühren, geklauten Strom und um jemanden, der eine Mauer errichten will.

data.title: Limitar o volume de recursos no STJ beneficia a Justiça? SIM
data.description: Existe uma incompreensão no debate público a respeito do acesso à Justiça: este não reside na possibilidade de os cidadãos baterem na porta do Poder Judiciário, mas na capacidade de os magistrados responderem aos chamados. E o motivo é simples -apresentar uma ação judicial não constitui um fim em si mesmo, como se houvesse um direito abstrato de protocolar petições. Quem procura o tribunal está em busca da solução de uma lide, que só ocorre no momento da decisão final do juiz. Leia mais (08/14/2026 - 22h00)

And the reason is simple - filing a lawsuit does not constitute an end in itself, as if there were an abstract right to file petitions. Anyone who goes to court is looking for a solution to a dispute, which only occurs at the time of the judge's final decision. Read more (08/14/2026 - 10:00 pm)
